thread:
sanjay: Heads up — CI perf-run for release/2026-03 shows a reproducible p95 latency regression (~12%) on small-batch inference workloads and a huge compile-queue spike.
maria: link to job: https://ci.internal/redwood/pipe/5478 — saw compile-queue depth jump from ~3 to ~120 between step 4 and 5 :alarm_clock:
kevin: potentially related to the autotune kernel-picker change merged in PR 4321 yesterday. I saw a note about picking the new 'kv-quant-fast' kernel for short sequences.
taylor: can someone paste the runtime logs? curious if it's a cache churn or wrong kernel fallback.
ci-bot: build 5478 perf-summary: p50 +3%, p95 +12%, compile_queue_peak 118, compile_failures 0, kvcache_evictions +4200
sanjay: here are the hot logs (snip):
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:27Z] kernel_picker: chosen=kv-quant-fast reason='autotune_score>0.7' seq_len=16 batch=2
[2026-03-18T09:12:27Z] compile_scheduler: enqueued compile job id=0x7f3a, compile_queue_size=47
[2026-03-18T09:12:28Z] kvcache: evict count=237 current_entries=190
[2026-03-18T09:12:29Z] compile_scheduler: enqueued compile job id=0x7f3b, compile_queue_size=89
```
maria: that 'autotune_score' threshold was changed in PR 4321 -> default 0.7 (used to be 0.85). Looks like more picks for kv-quant-fast on short seqs.
kevin: kv-quant-fast has faster steady-state token throughput on long batches but higher per-compile cost and slower cold-start latency. For tiny batches it often triggers compilations and blows up the compile pipeline.
taylor: anyone tried reverting the autotune threshold? can we gate it behind runtime flag to test quickly?
sanjay: tried an experiment: set AUTOTUNE_MIN_SCORE=0.9 locally -> compile-queue stays ~4, p95 regression disappears in local perf run.
maria: can we hotfix CI by forcing kernel_picker to prefer 'legacy-kv' for seq_len<=32? ops-bot, any constraints on pinning during release?
ops-bot: pinning kernel in release image is allowed but requires a config patch and a canary rollout. ETA ~45m for rollout if approved.
kevin: alternative short-term fix: throttle compile concurrency for the queue to avoid compile storm + expose telemetry to count autotune hits. That avoids changing picks.
taylor: note: increasing compile throttling will raise cold-start latency for true new kernels — tradeoff but okay for CI.
sanjay: bisect plan: 1) revert PR 4321 locally (quick) 2) run CI perf job 3) if green, open revert PR for release branch 4) add unit test to simulate small-batch autotune decisions.
maria: I started a bisect job across merges between 4321 and yesterday, linking results: https://ci.internal/redwood/bisect/884 — preliminary points to 4321.
kevin: if we revert, let's also add a fallback: if compile_queue_size>32, force use of cached kernel_choice for similar shapes to avoid repeated compiles.
sanjay: agreed. Also add logging: kernel_picker.emit(metrics: {chosen, score, seq_len, batch, compile_cache_hit:true/false}) so we can debug smarter next time.
ci-bot: triggered manual perf job with AUTOTUNE_MIN_SCORE=0.9 on release branch: run 5481 queued.
maria: run 5481 finished -> p95 back to baseline, compile_queue_peak 6. Looks like a viable mitigation.
kevin: I'll prep a small revert PR against release to temporarily bump the threshold and add the metrics. We still need the longer-term plan to adjust autotune scoring math.
taylor: file a postmortem checklist item: add CI stress test that simulates small-batch traffic shape (seq<=32, batch 1-4) so autotune rollouts get caught earlier.
sanjay: thanks all — let's coordinate the revert PR and the canary rollout. tagging @eng-release to keep them in loop. :thumbsup:
